chunks: Praise be to Allah, the Manifest to His creation through His creation, and the Apparent to their hearts through His Proof,

He created the creation without deliberation, since deliberation does not befit except those with thinking organs, while He has no thinking organ in Himself. His knowledge pierces the inner hiddenness of the veils, and encompasses the obscurity of the core beliefs.
ai.seo_question: How does Allah's creation differ from human deliberation according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha highlights Allah's absolute self-sufficiency (Al-Ghani) by contrasting His effortless creation with human deliberation (rawiyyah), which implies need and limitation. It underscores the concept of Divine Knowledge (Ilm) penetrating the innermost secrets (sirriyat), a theme central to Shia theological discussions on God's transcendence beyond physical or mental constraints. This description serves as a foundation for understanding divine authority during times of historical vicissitudes, reminding believers that God's insight into hidden realities remains unshaken despite external changes.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Praise be to Allāh Who is Manifest before His creation because of themselves. Who is apparent to their hearts because of clear Proof;

who created without meditating, since meditating does not befit except one who has thinking organs while He has no thinking organ in Himself. His knowledge has split forth the inside of unknown secrets and covered the bottom of deep beliefs.
